issue.title: src/unit_test.c: help text says unknown args are "ignored" but they cause EXIT_FAILURE
issue.body:
The help text in `src/unit_test.c` states:

> Unknown arguments are reported but ignored.

However, `parse_arg()` returns `-1` when it encounters an unknown key:

```c
/* Unknown key: report just so typos don't silently pass. */
fprintf(stderr, "Unknown argument '-%s=%s'\n", key, value);
return -1;
```

This propagates through `read_args()` and causes `tf_init()` to return `EXIT_FAILURE`, terminating the program before any tests run.

Windows/MSVC build):

```
> tests.exe --typo=1
Unknown argument '-typo=1'
> echo $LASTEXITCODE
1
```

vs. a valid argument, which runs normally:

```
> tests.exe -i=1
...
Total execution time: 38.234 seconds
> echo $LASTEXITCODE
0
```

Given the comment in `parse_arg()` ("report just so typos don't silently pass"), the fail-fast behavior looks intentional — in which case the fix
is just updating the help text. But I wanted to check before opening a PR: should the **documentation** be corrected to match the actual
(fail-fast) behavior, or should the **behavior** be changed to match the documented "ignored" claim.
